title: DB keeps life fractional while truncating period/month, rounds rate via decimal ROUND, and flushes subnormal steps
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20430, DB(cost, salvage, life, period, [month]) truncates period and month toward zero while leaving life fractional (so DB(1000, 100, 0.5, 0.25, 1) computes rate = 1 - (100/1000)^(1/0.5) = 0.99 and returns 82.5). The depreciation rate is rounded to 3 decimal places using Excel's 15-significant-digit decimal ROUND rule, integer-power exponents below u32::MAX use an x87 loop, an overflowing exp/log rate power yielding NaN produces rate 0, and each period's depreciation is flushed from subnormals to 0 before updating book value. All 2,034 full-bank DB rows match.
basis: Measured across CalcFunc-Evidence cache/w111-depreciation-20260929/answers-db.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and Excel 16.0.20527.20088 (f3_financial row 7); 2,034/2,034 full-bank rows match.
